hypothesis: Incrementally completing rows around two allocated differences with local difference-disjoint checks will make multi-anchor allocation computationally viable and permit a meaningful exact-cover search that the rejection-based pair generator could not reach.
rationale: The prior pair-conditioned method spent 120 seconds rejecting 3,893,999 full random samples and never entered exact-cover search. Incremental completion prunes duplicate differences after each added mark, and a bounded random subset of pair anchors avoids the exhaustive all-pair scheduling bottleneck while retaining the multi-anchor structural hypothesis.
expected_information_gain: Separates the pair-allocation idea from the prior generator's implementation bottleneck and tests whether multi-anchor rows can exceed the established depth-five ceiling.
method: Shuffle all unordered pairs of differences 1..111, process the first 500 pairs, and generate up to 30 rows per pair. For each pair, fix the two positive marks, then recursively add three marks, rejecting any extension that creates an intra-row duplicate or reuses an existing row difference. Deduplicate valid rows by exact difference mask. Run the existing scarcity-aware exact-cover recursion with 24 rare-anchor probes, a six-gap budget, and independent integer verification of any complete assignment.
metric: completed pair anchors, valid and deduplicated rows, exact-cover nodes, maximum assembled depth, omitted-difference count, target assignment, and independent DTS validity
metric_relation_to_true_objective: A complete seven-row assignment accepted by the independent integer validator is exactly a true-objective scope<=111 witness; generation counts and partial depth are finite-family diagnostics only.

configuration.cover_branching: fewest currently compatible rows among statically rare uncovered differences plus six-gap budget

kill_condition: Stop at the first independently validated target witness, completion of the 500-pair finite schedule, 120-second wall budget, or 2,000,000 search nodes. Do not infer global impossibility from finite catalog failure.

baseline_comparison.expected_relation: strict improvement only if complete and validator-valid

previous_best_comparison.pair_allocation: 3278 rows; generation ended before exact-cover search
previous_best_comparison.expected_relation: same multi-anchor hypothesis with incremental completion and bounded pair schedule

interpretation: The incremental pair generator still consumed the full 120-second budget before exact-cover search, despite producing 14,397 valid masks. No depth or target conclusion is available.
what_was_learned: Incremental local pruning was insufficient: 37.5 million attempts were required for 14,400 valid rows, and the search phase received zero nodes. The fixed-pair completion representation is not viable under this budget.
recommended_next_action: Close fixed-pair generation. Reallocate to a row-library packing search that directly optimizes disjoint difference masks, or to algebraic construction reasoning; do not repeat this generator without a different constructive mechanism.
repetition_justification: This changes the row-construction mechanism from full-sample rejection to incremental constraint propagation and limits pair scheduling to a finite randomized subset; it is not a seed or budget repeat of the failed all-pairs implementation.
